author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Twenty-five years after the September 11 attacks, the changes they triggered still shape everyday life in the United States. The attacks led to the creation of the Transportation Security Administration, subjecting air travellers to tougher screening. Weeks later, Congress passed the Patriot Act, giving the government sweeping new surveillance powers, including access to phone, email, financial and other records.

The attacks also exposed failures in how agencies shared information, leading to the creation of the Department of Homeland Security, which brought 22 federal agencies under one roof, and an overhaul of immigration enforcement that produced Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE.

Al Jazeera's Kristen Saloomey reports from New York.

The United Nations says more than 23,000 people have been displaced from the two localities since August 11. The humanitarian situation is worsening as the rainy season makes conditions at displacement sites increasingly difficult.

Many families are struggling without adequate shelter, food or drinking water. Heavy rain has turned the clay-rich ground into mud, making it difficult for displaced people to move and humanitarian workers to provide shelter and sanitation.

As fighting continues in southeastern Blue Nile, more people are arriving in Damazin in need of shelter, food, water, healthcare and other basic services.

Al Jazeera’s Almigdad Alruhaid reports.

description:
The second day of the republican convention is underway in Dallas, Texas ahead of the US midterm elections.
Trump made a pledge on Wednesday to give every American adult $5,000 if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in November. 

Al Jazeera’s Richard Gaisford has been to a small Texan town to gauge reaction and found not all Republicans are in favour of it.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Former US Ambassador to Algeria and former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State, Henry Ensher, says Yemen’s Houthis could take control of the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait, and that the US lacks the capacity to stop it from happening.

Henry Ensher told Al Jazeera that the Iran-backed group wants to at least threaten the important trade route for its own purposes and as a consequence of its alliance with Tehran. He said he was “surprised that this hasn’t happened” before.

“It may well be that the Iranians and the Houthis were just building their capabilities before they made their move,” he said.

He said the US, which has committed 20 ships to enforcing its blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, would “hope that somebody else – the Saudis and their new alliance partners, potentially the Israelis – will take care of this particular problem,” he said.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guard says its navy struck a US-operated surface drone at the entrance of the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranians claim to have ‘thwarted an aggressive mission’ using the drone, which is shaped like a sail boat. Washington has yet to comment on the claim.
